feature_order_note: Input to predict() must be a DataFrame with columns in this exact order.
preprocessing: StandardScaler fitted on training-period data only (1990-2007). Applied identically to test data.
selection_criterion: Lowest mean CV RMSE across 5 season-aware expanding-window folds.

evaluation_strategy.split_type: Chronological holdout with season-aware expanding-window CV
evaluation_strategy.cv_method: Custom season-aware expanding-window (5 folds, 2 validation seasons each)
evaluation_strategy.cv_note: 2004 absent from all folds (NHL season cancelled due to labour lockout).

cv_metrics.sd_note: Standard deviations reflect variation across 5 folds, not confidence intervals.

cv_to_test_diff_note: Signed difference: test RMSE minus mean CV RMSE. Negative = better on test than CV average.
assumptions_and_limitations: Win_Pct is treated as a continuous regression target; the pipeline does not clip predictions to [0, 1].
Features (Goals_For, Goals_Against, Year) are all end-of-season totals; mid-season or pre-season prediction is not supported.
OT_Losses is excluded: its 224 missing values (pre-shootout era) are irrelevant since the column is not used.
Year is included as a numeric feature to capture structural era effects; it is not a proxy for a time index.
The dataset covers 1990–2011 only. Extrapolation beyond this window should be done with caution.
Positive serial autocorrelation in residuals (Durbin-Watson ≈ 1.08, documented in statistical analysis section) is not corrected by this model.
The model is the best among five evaluated models under this specific validation strategy. It is not claimed to be globally optimal.
